source: Native AWS Lambda SQS fresh-policy authorization corpus: two completed experiments plus one cleaned setup failure

findings.observed: Both fresh-role cases rejected CreateEventSourceMapping twice with InvalidParameterValueException and exact message: The function execution role does not have permissions to call GetQueueAttributes on SQS. ReceiveMessage and DeleteMessage remained allowed.
findings.scope: Admission evidence; no mapping was admitted and therefore no denied-case background poller existed.

findings.boundary: Role versus queue explicit ReceiveMessage/DeleteMessage denies
findings.observed: All four fresh contexts rejected mapping creation twice, naming ReceiveMessage or DeleteMessage respectively; resource-policy denials were not ignored at admission.
findings.scope: Queue deny targeted the fresh execution-role ARN, not the operator. No denial context permitted mapping creation in this experiment.

findings.observed: Allowing all three source actions only under Null lambda:SourceFunctionArn=true admitted the mapping and delivered source message ef5e9aea-661a-4ed0-b13a-d209ebb6675c to request 80e2df0d-7e71-566f-a59e-bc2e0b040d4b with ApproximateReceiveCount=1. ArnEquals to the actual unqualified function ARN instead rejected admission twice naming ReceiveMessage.

Both directly invoked fresh context functions successfully SendMessage under ArnEquals to their own unqualified ARN and received AccessDenied under Null=true to another owned sink. The actual SQS-triggered invocation repeated the same success/denial pair. Sink actor receive recovered successful direct-send ID fe7eb25e-2a4b-4b95-9f0e-d0abcc7da358.
findings.scope: Three successful SDK SendMessage response IDs captured; bounded sink receive recovered one, not an exhaustive sink drain.

findings.boundary: Minimal observed source policy positive delivery
findings.observed: A separate fresh role allowed only sqs:ReceiveMessage, sqs:DeleteMessage, sqs:GetQueueAttributes on its exact source ARN, plus logs:CreateLogStream/PutLogEvents on its precreated owned log group. No other SQS permission or source resource policy. Mapping admitted and source 6fd6ca59-cd7c-42ee-b581-5b3ea57b1154 arrived in request 8ebcfb38-1994-5a20-b298-981b6f3f90fd with ApproximateReceiveCount=1. Later approximate source counts zero and two actor receives after mapping absence plus 25-second visibility recovery found no message.
findings.scope: Positive runtime plus bounded queue evidence; no direct DeleteMessage audit was collected.

findings.observed: All ten source-absent and four minimal-positive background GetEventSourceMapping responses were Enabled with StateTransitionReason=USER_INITIATED and omitted LastProcessingResult.
findings.scope: Do not synthesize a successful LastProcessingResult field from these observations.

uncertainties: Fresh queue policy Principal ARN set initially failed InvalidAttributeValue, then identical inputs succeeded after 10 seconds in each resource-deny case. This is consistent with principal propagation but is not proof of its internal cause; the initially aborted run is retained and cleaned.

Execution-role policies were never edited after initial attachment. Main-run first admission ages were 75.99–95.70 seconds since attachment; negative retries were 109.61–133.70 seconds. Minimal positive first admission was 63.81 seconds. These measured windows are not universal stabilization guarantees.

No tested deny permitted admission, so this does not establish behavior for policies changed after mapping creation, existing poller credential caches, or runtime-only DeleteMessage denial. No in-place IAM mutation was used.

No CloudTrail source API audit was collected. SourceFunctionArn context is demonstrated through positive/negative conditional policy behavior, not direct credential-context inspection. Queue drain supports acknowledgement but is not an exact DeleteMessage request trace.

Background sampling windows after the unchanged-policy retry were 235.31 seconds in the eight-case run and 61.31 seconds in the minimal-positive run; source sends preceded those windows. Approximate queue counts visibly lagged successful runtime delivery and cannot be treated as precise live counts.

Post-mapping actor recovery used VisibilityTimeout=0 and MaxNumberOfMessages=10. Each denied source returned the same exact ID repeatedly with counts 1..10 in the first API response and 11..20 in the second. These are actor-created receives, not Lambda retries; all receipts and ordering are retained. No general batch-packing inference is made.
The operator had existing default account permissions; account/SCP context was not inventoried or changed. Claims are limited to these same-account, unencrypted standard queues and explicit policies.
production_implications: Observed admission behavior supports retaining GetQueueAttributes in CheckConsumeQueue; the previously unisolated omission case now has explicit native evidence.
Both identity and queue resource policies matter to admission for the isolated ReceiveMessage/DeleteMessage denies; exact errors name the denied action.
Keep event-source poller role context separate from function-runtime credentials: only runtime code carries lambda:SourceFunctionArn in the observed SQS condition cases.

The shared CheckConsumeQueue call before every local polling batch is not independently justified by this admission-focused experiment; do not infer native repeated preflight or cached-policy refresh behavior from it.

cleanup.proof: Per-run ordered cleanup-absence observations include exact-name queue/function/role lookups, exact-match filtered log-group lists, and mapping GetEventSourceMapping ResourceNotFoundException; all owned objects absent.
